What pass requires: If the teacher confirmed IM: lesson uses the Launch → Explore → Discuss → Synthesize structure with IM routine names. If another curriculum is named: the lesson matches that curriculum's instructional model. If no curriculum is named: any coherent research-based structure passes — a generic four-phase arc is fine and is NOT a violation — so long as no curriculum-proprietary terminology appears. Fail = IM terminology for a non-IM teacher, or a named curriculum's instructional model ignored.

Criterion: Unknown positions in all three locations
What pass requires: For K–5 standards where CGI applies: practice problems and the exit ticket include result-unknown, change-unknown, AND start-unknown problems. Pass = all three present. Fail = only result-unknown, or start-unknown is absent.
Notes: Only applies to K–5 CGI standards

Criterion: Exit ticket targets start-unknown or the structurally hardest case
What pass requires: For K–5 CGI standards: exit ticket uses a start-unknown problem. For 6–12 standards: exit ticket targets the case most likely to cause confusion (e.g., right-shift for transformations, multiplicative form for one-step equations). Pass = hard case targeted. Fail = easy case used.

Math misconceptions must name the wrong equation form vs. the correct one (e.g., 'student writes 45 + ? = 18 instead of 45 − 18 = ?'), not describe a general confusion pattern. Pass = at least 2 of 3 misconceptions include a specific wrong form. Fail = all misconceptions are general pattern descriptions.

Criterion: Discuss phase with student-to-student talk moves
What pass requires: The lesson includes a dedicated Discuss/Synthesize phase with at least 10 minutes allocated, embedding at least one NAMED talk move (e.g., turn-and-talk, revoicing, agree/disagree, partner compare, think-pair-share) — and at least one named move is a student-to-student interaction. Fail = no discussion phase, under 10 minutes, no named talk move, or a discussion that is entirely teacher-led questioning.

Criterion: Problem set covers the standard's structural variety
What pass requires: FIRST enumerate the structural cases of the target standard yourself (e.g., unknown positions for operations word problems, transformation types, proportional vs. non-proportional cases). THEN verify every enumerated case appears in the practice problems or exit ticket. List the enumeration and where each case appears in the explanation. Fail = any structural case of the standard is absent from the problem set.

Criterion: Standard's full numerical scope is used
What pass requires: If the standard specifies rational numbers, at least one problem uses decimals or fractions. If the standard specifies 'within 100', problems use numbers throughout that range, not just single digits. Pass = numerical scope matches the standard. Fail = only whole numbers when rational required, or only small numbers when the standard specifies a larger range.
